sources.title: Cambodia Tourism Ministry's January trial announcement
sources.publisher: Agence Kampuchea Presse, Ministry of Information, Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual 16 January 2026 government publication read in full. AKP is Cambodia's state news agency under the Ministry of Information; its article directly reports and quotes the Ministry of Tourism statement dated 15 January, including passport scope, dates and conditions. This is a recovered government publication, not a fresh verification of the inaccessible eVisa or Tourism Ministry URLs.

sources.title: Cambodia launches trial visa-free entry through October 15
sources.publisher: Agence Kampuchea Presse, Ministry of Information, Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual government publication dated 15 June 2026 read in full. It confirms that the trial launched that day, identifies its October endpoint and expressly describes the per-visit stay and multiple-entry treatment, alongside the Tourism Minister's launch remarks.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Eligible travellers will be permitted to stay for up to 14 days per visit

sources.title: PRC Embassy consular reminder for visa-free Cambodia travel
sources.publisher: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual 20 June 2026 consular notice read on the official Chinese embassy domain. Its opening paragraph expressly identifies ordinary PRC passports, the trial dates, departure from China or a third country, multiple entries and a fourteen-day single stay. Used as passport-issuer corroboration alongside destination-government publications, not as the sole destination authority.

sources.title: Macao DSI notice of Cambodia's June–October trial

sources.officialityEvidence: Actual 12 June 2026 Identification Services Bureau notice read on the Macao Government Information Bureau's official portal. policies.title: Cambodia's temporary Chinese tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: Ordinary mainland Chinese, Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport holders may visit Cambodia visa-free for up to 14 days per entry during the trial from 15 June through 15 October 2026. Multiple entries are permitted and the e-Arrival Card remains required. No post-trial access status is established by this review.
conditions: This record covers ordinary tourist visits under the temporary programme, not employment, residence or other travel documents. The destination-government announcement expressly includes mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao and excludes Taiwan.

Eligible passport holders may travel directly from China or from another country. The announced exemption does not require a visa application or visa fee, and multiple entries are permitted during the trial.

Travellers must complete Cambodia's e-Arrival Card. This arrival declaration does not turn the expressly visa-free programme into an ETA. No universal advance-only submission deadline is asserted here.

The supported trial ends on 15 October 2026. An August government report describes a private-sector request for a year-end extension, not an adopted extension. These sources do not establish the status for a new entry from 16 October 2026; continued visa-free access or a specific replacement visa route must not be inferred.

allowedStays.label: Up to 14 days per entry during the trial
notes: Multiple entries are permitted during the trial; the fourteen-day allowance is per entry, not an aggregate four-month allowance.

The sources do not settle how a stay following an entry near 15 October interacts with the programme endpoint. This record does not promise a stay beyond that endpoint or treat 16 October as an automatic departure deadline for an already admitted traveller.
